title: Emergency stop and interlocks in Ladder
summary: Make a running line stop when the emergency stop is pressed, show it with the red light and refuse to restart until Start is pressed again.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Stop every output while the emergency stop is pressed.
Remember the stop, so that releasing the button does not restart the line.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: The starting program in src/ThreeLevelLifts.ld.json draws the line and has no stop. While the emergency stop is pressed, every belt and lift must be off and the red lamp lit; the line must stay stopped when the button is released and run again only after a new press of Start.
stages.checkpoint: You can say which outputs must be off during the stop, what Red must show, and what must still be true after the button is released.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, follow the stop: at 15.5 s the emergency stop is pressed while a lift may be moving; the line must stop, stay stopped when the button is released at 17 s, and run again only after the Start press at 17.5 s.
stages.checkpoint: Red on and every output off at 16 s; still stopped at 17.3 s; Red off and the line running again after Start.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}: The starter ignores the emergency stop, so the line keeps running; stop every output while EStopOk is FALSE, light Red, keep the line stopped after the release and run it again only with a new press of Start.
stages.checkpoint: Check reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the plant move, press Run (F5) and open the 3D view.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named estop-interlocks and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the stack light turn red and the belts and lifts stop when the scenario presses the emergency stop, and run again after Start.
stages.checkpoint: Red stays on after the release until Start, and the outputs fall in the same scan as EStopOk.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The AT assertions pin the stop at 16 s, the held stop at 17.3 s and the restart at 18 s; the interlocks that were already in the program are the same idea as in the 2.0 lesson interlock-guard-permissive.
stages.checkpoint: This stop is only what the program does with the EStopOk signal: it is not an emergency-stop circuit and it gives no stopping time. The grade cannot see a lift that keeps rising a little after the stop.

hints.text: Look at 17.3 s, after the button is released: EStopOk is TRUE again, yet Red is still lit and the outputs are still off. Which variable of your program can say that, and what makes it change?

Add a local BOOL variable Stopped. Draw the Start rungs first: with a normally open contact of Start in series with one of EStopOk, one rung sets Active and another resets Stopped. Then draw the stop rungs after them: with a normally closed contact of EStopOk, one rung sets Stopped and another resets Active, so the stop wins in the same scan. Light Red from Stopped with a contact and a coil. Every output already depends on Active, so no output needs its own stop logic.

faultCases: The starter ignores the emergency stop, so the line keeps running; stop every output while EStopOk is FALSE, light Red, keep the line stopped after the release and run it again only with a new press of Start.
